method: Visual inspection of the published chart image (data/digitized/ramesh-2013/figure2-vas.jpg); NOT pixel-calibrated digitization. This is a 4-line overlapping time-course chart per panel (0/2/4/6 puffs) with 7 timepoints (15,30,60,90,120,180,210 min) and overlapping SEM error bars, which is a HIGH-ambiguity chart type -- the 2/4/6-puff markers frequently overlap or sit within one SEM of each other, making it genuinely hard to attribute a given marker to the correct condition at several timepoints (this overlap is itself the paper's finding: these conditions are not dose-dependent). Values below are best-effort per-condition reads where the marker was reasonably distinguishable, with confidence notes where it was not.
confidence: low-to-moderate and NOT uniform across conditions -- see per-series notes. Do not treat 2-vs-4-vs-6 differences below as reliable; do treat the 0-vs-active separation and the overall declining time-course shape as reliable.
priority_note: This is the primary series for Exhibit 001's 'high' track. Recommend re-digitizing with an actual calibrated tool (WebPlotDigitizer) using the original high-resolution image before this data ships in a production exhibit -- these estimates are adequate for prototyping the interaction (slider behavior, chart layout) but not as the final source of truth.

panels.confidence: moderate for 0-puffs (clearly separated, low overlap); low for distinguishing 2 vs 4 vs 6 puffs (markers cluster tightly, especially t>=60)
moderate for 0-puffs; low for distinguishing 2 vs 4 vs 6 puffs

cross_check: 0-puffs << active-puffs separation, and the 'active conditions largely overlap each other' shape, are consistent with the exact text-reported findings (ramesh-2013-vas-high-not-dose-dependent): 'high' and 'stimulated' increase vs 0 puffs (p<=.001 and p<=.05 respectively) but are not dose-dependent among active conditions -- the visual clustering IS the finding, not a reading error.
